description: A dermatofibroma is a common, benign fibrous skin nodule formed by a proliferation of fibrohistiocytic cells within the dermis, most often found on the lower legs. It is typically a small, firm, solitary growth that is harmless and usually asymptomatic, and does not give rise to cancer.
symptoms: Firm, well-circumscribed nodule, usually 0.5-1.5 cm in diameter
Pink to light brown color on lighter skin, dark brown to black on darker skin; sometimes paler in the center
Feels like a small stone under, or slightly raised above, the skin surface
Tethered to the skin surface but mobile over underlying tissue
Characteristic "dimple sign" (or "pinch sign"): the overlying skin dimples inward when the nodule is pinched
Usually asymptomatic, but sometimes painful, tender, or itchy
More common in adults, and more common in women than men
warning_signs: Asymmetrical structures or colors on dermoscopy
Large size or discomfort warranting professional assessment
recommendation: Usually only reassurance is needed, since dermatofibroma does not become cancerous. A dermatologist may recommend biopsy or excision if atypical features (recent enlargement, ulceration, dermoscopic asymmetry) are present, primarily to rule out look-alike conditions such as dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans or desmoplastic melanoma rather than because the dermatofibroma itself has changed. Surgical removal is optional if the lesion is a cosmetic nuisance, though recurrence after removal is common.
